1.why: /api/verify-token requires token.sessionId === session.id and matches the stored mockAccountHash, so the code is bound to the requesting session/account, though the 'user' is only a single mock account.

2.why: A token is rejected unless token.sessionId matches the current session id, so another visitor's session cannot use someone else's reset code.

3.why: Nothing rotates or invalidates the recovery_session cookie or any other session after /api/reset-password succeeds — the same session id continues to be used for MFA and later steps.

4.why: Bun.serve is configured with TLS cert/key, HSTS is sent, and the plain-HTTP listener 308-redirects to HTTPS, though no explicit minimum TLS version is pinned (relies on Bun defaults).

5.why: Reset tokens are stored only as SHA-256 hashes, rate-limit keys hash the client address, and passwords use Bun bcrypt (cost 10); these are appropriate, though hashing rather than encryption and no data-at-rest encryption exists.

6.why: There is no real email delivery at all; the 'recovery message' mock returns the raw token in the JSON response and prints it to the page log, so no email-level protection of private data is demonstrated.

7.why: Identifier, token, MFA code and password all pass strict regex/length/policy validation server-side, JSON body type is checked, and all client rendering uses textContent.

8.why: The only redirect is a fixed 308 to https://localhost:PORT/, and the simulated verification link is a same-origin /verify?token= with encodeURIComponent — no user-controlled redirect targets.

9.why: No email templates exist; the simulated delivery strings contain only the generated token and are inserted via textContent, so no scripts or user-supplied HTML appear.

10.why: Error responses are generic and stack-trace free, but the raw recovery token and the MFA code are deliberately written to the console and mirrored into the on-page <pre id="logs"> element.

11.why: Passwords are bcrypt-hashed and never persisted in plaintext, but MOCK_MFA_CODE = "482916" is a secret hardcoded in the source and returned to the client.

12.why: There are no default accounts or login credentials in the app, yet the fixed, hardcoded MFA code 482916 functions as a default static secret for every reset.

13.why: Server-wide, address-keyed rate limits cap recovery requests at 3 and token/MFA verification failures at 5 per 10-minute window, returning 429 thereafter.

14.why: /api/recovery-request always returns the same generic 'If the details match an account...' message and issues a token regardless of the identifier, preventing enumeration.

15.why: The reset code is randomBytes(32) base64url, stored only as a SHA-256 hash, single-use, 10-minute TTL, and bound to the issuing session id.
